scope: Developer experience, CI, packaging, and release-control plan only. No application implementation, CI workflow, package, signing, deployment, or public release is approved or created.

dependencyEvidence.sharedBusinessRuleBoundary: Download states, retry, resume, cancellation, destination conflict, finalization, and recovery rules belong to one shared domain or service implementation. Desktop UI, browser, filesystem, network, CLI, packaging, and test adapters consume that implementation and may not duplicate or redefine those rules.

proposedLayout.purpose: UI-independent state machine, policies, commands, events, validation, and error taxonomy
HTTP transfer and integrity adapter implementing ports owned by the download domain
Thin desktop composition root and UI for an approved platform and framework
Filesystem, persistence, notifications, and file-reveal interfaces plus platform adapters
Adapter conformance against the shared domain contract
Deterministic network, storage, restart, and package scenarios

entryCriteria: A dated decision from sepehr-product-owner approves the first platform, supported versions, MVP behaviors, exclusions, and meaning of native and all devices.
The desktop foundation, implementation language, package manager, test runner, persistence choice, and packaging channel are approved.
Open-source license and third-party dependency rules are approved before dependencies or public source-distribution claims are added.

localCommands.status: templates only; exact commands are blocked until the toolchain is selected
localCommands.constraint: Expose these operations through one documented repository runner so local and CI execution use the same locked commands.

continuousIntegration.reason: There is no approved implementation stack, dependency lockfile, executable source, or test runner; a workflow now would be speculative and could falsely imply implementation readiness.
pullRequestGates: Formatting, linting, type checking, unit tests, and shared-domain contract tests
Deterministic adversarial network and restart-recovery integration tests
Dependency license policy, vulnerability scan, secret scan, and generated-artifact integrity checks
Platform UI accessibility tests in a real DOM or equivalent desktop runtime when user-visible behavior exists
Resource-budget tests for concurrency, CPU, memory, disk, and network after budgets are approved
runnerPolicy: Use pinned runner images and pinned action or tool revisions; mutable latest tags are prohibited.
Give pull-request jobs read-only repository permissions and no signing, publishing, production, or long-lived credentials.
Treat forked and untrusted pull requests as credential-free; do not execute privileged release jobs from untrusted code.
Run platform-specific filesystem, accessibility, install, and package tests on each approved operating system.
Upload test evidence with bounded retention and without raw URLs, credentials, headers, destination paths, or downloaded content.
requiredEvidence: runner operating system and image identity

releasePipeline.production: Not declared. Production deployment or public distribution requires separate attributed human approval.

stages.name: build
requirements: Build from a reviewed canonical revision
Use locked inputs on a pinned platform runner
Produce unsigned immutable artifacts and checksums

stages.name: verify
requirements: Run unit, contract, integration, accessibility, resilience, performance, security, install, upgrade, rollback, and uninstall checks applicable to the approved platform

stages.name: stage
requirements: Promote the exact verified artifact without rebuilding
Attach SBOM, provenance, license inventory, checksums, and verification evidence

stages.name: sign-and-publish
requirements: Use an assigned release approver and signing-key custodian
Verify signatures and rollback instructions before publication

releasePipeline.immutablePromotionRule: A content-addressed artifact is built once and promoted through verification and staging. Rebuilding invalidates prior evidence and requires re-verification.
releasePipeline.releaseTrigger: A protected, attributable release action against a verified canonical revision; never a pull-request event.
releasePipeline.rollback: Every distribution channel must document revocation, rollback, supported downgrade behavior, and owner escalation before its first binary release.

dependencyPolicy: Commit and enforce the selected ecosystem lockfile
Allow dependencies only under the approved open-source policy
Review transitive licenses and native binary provenance
Automate vulnerability review with an accountable exception and expiry process
artifactPolicy: Generate an SBOM and provenance bound to artifact checksums
Scan packages before and after signing
Retain evidence sufficient to reproduce or explain the build
Do not claim reproducibility until independent repeated-build evidence exists
secretPolicy: No secrets in repository, logs, test fixtures, artifacts, or pull-request jobs
Signing identities remain outside ordinary CI and are accessed only by audited release jobs
Use short-lived identity federation where supported
Document rotation, revocation, recovery, and emergency release procedures
supplyChainAndSecrets.privacyPolicy: Telemetry is absent by default. Diagnostics must redact sensitive URL components, credentials, headers, cookies, local paths, and file contents.

onboardingDefinition: Supported host platform and tool versions
One bootstrap command after toolchain selection
One deterministic sample download fixture served locally
Troubleshooting for proxy, certificate, filesystem, and platform packaging failures

testPyramid.focus: Pure state transitions, policies, invariants, and property-based sequences
Persistence, filesystem, transfer, and platform adapters against shared ports
Ranges, redirects, identity changes, interruption, insufficient space, restart, and finalization integrity
Keyboard, focus, assistive-technology labeling, reduced motion, package lifecycle, and core user journey
testPyramid.environment: real DOM or equivalent approved desktop runtime

developerWorkflow.fixtureSafety: Test servers and fixtures use generated non-sensitive data, loopback or isolated test networks, bounded file sizes, and temporary destinations; production data and credentials are prohibited.

releaseReadinessChecklist.gate: License, contribution governance, vulnerability reporting, and release ownership
Platform package, signing identity, key custody, update, and rollback ownership

traceability.limitation: No shared domain implementation or executable scenarios exist.
Platform and toolchain selections remain unapproved.
The record defines gates but does not constitute approval of license, governance, signing, or release ownership.
No UI exists; runtime accessibility results are unavailable.
MVP capability classification remains a product decision.
Independent disposition is reserved for ENG-15 and no release-readiness claim is made.

implementationNotes: No CI workflow was added because an executable stack and locked command contract do not yet exist.
When implementation starts, business rules must be implemented once in the shared download domain or service and consumed by every UI and adapter.
User-visible behavior must be verified in a real DOM, browser, integration, or equivalent desktop runtime; source-pattern checks are insufficient.
No production credentials, production data, database operation, deployment, signing action, branch, or commit was used.
knownRisks: Missing product, platform, UI foundation, language, package manager, persistence, and packaging decisions prevent creation of truthful executable automation.
License, dependency policy, governance, vulnerability reporting, release ownership, and signing custody remain unresolved blockers to public source or binary release.
CI configuration can create a privileged supply-chain path; untrusted pull requests must remain isolated from secrets and release permissions.
Cross-platform packaging, signing, filesystem, accessibility, and rollback behavior requires native runners and platform owners.
No source, lockfile, tests, package, or runtime exists, so quality, security, resilience, accessibility, performance, and reproducibility claims cannot be made.
Independent verification remains outstanding and may only be issued by ENG-15.
